contests.title: Central Community Unit School District 4 — At-large board elections

provenance.quote:
Shall members of the Board of Education of Central
Community Unit School District No. 4, Iroquois and
Kankakee Counties, Illinois, be elected in 2029 and
thereafter, at large and without restriction by area of
residence within the district instead of the current
restriction that not more than three (3) members of
the board of education may be selected from one
(1) congressional township in the school district?

Shall the Road District of the Township of
Bourbonnais be abolished, with all rights, powers,
duties, assets, property, liabilities, obligations, and
responsibilities being assumed by the Township of
Bourbonnais?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Elects Orion Community Unit School District 223 board members at large instead of by area of residence within the district.
measureRecords.noMeans: Keep the existing residence-area election arrangement.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Elects Rockridge Community Unit School District 300 board members at large instead of by area of residence within the district.
measureRecords.noMeans: Keep the existing residence-area election arrangement.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Beginning with 2029 elections, elects Central Community Unit School District 4 board members at large without residence-area restrictions. It replaces the current rule limiting the board to three members from any one congressional township in the district.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt unrestricted at-large board elections starting in 2029.
measureRecords.noMeans: Keep the current restriction of no more than three board members from one congressional township.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Abolishes Bourbonnais Township’s Road District and transfers all its rights, powers, duties, assets, property, liabilities, obligations and responsibilities to the township.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Abolish the Road District and transfer its functions and obligations to the township.
measureRecords.noMeans: Keep the Road District rather than abolish it through this question.
